To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chronic administration of morphine to rats increases the efficacy of opioid agonists to presynaptically inhibit GABAergic nerve terminal neurotransmitter release in periaqueduct gray (PAG) by an enhanced coupling to protein kinase A (PKA) signaling pathways.
opioid dependence enhances opioid efficacy in the periaquductedal gray area via a protein kinase A-dependent mechanism.

opioid dependence enhances the efficacy of μ-opioid agonists at presynaptic inhibitory GABAergic nerve endings in the periaquductal gray area (the brain's primary site for opioid analgesia) via an adenylyl-cyclase/protein kinase A-dependent mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and molecular adaptations of neurons in the central nervous system (CNS) that underlie opioid tolerance and dependence, and the behavioral consequences of these changes.
the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the development of tolerance and dependence to opioid drugs.
the cellular and molecular mechanisms of opioid tolerance and dependence and the role of these mechanisms in the development of withdrawal behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic morphine administration causes a change in the coupling of the μ-receptor to the GABAergic synapse that is mediated by a protein kinase A-dependent process.
opioid withdrawal enhances the efficacy of opioid agonists in PAG by increasing the sensitivity of GABAergic nerve endings to opioid inhibition.

opioid dependence induces an efficacious coupling of mu-opioid receptors to presynaptic inhibitory mechanisms in GABAergic neurons of the periaquedutcal gray area via adenylycylase- and protein kinases-dependent mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
opioid dependence induces a functional uncoupling between μ-receptors on presynaptic terminals and the inhibitory G protein (Gi/o) that is responsible for presynaptic inhibition.
opioid tolerance and dependence are mediated, in part, by a shift in the signal transduction pathway of the μ-opioid receptor.

opioid withdrawal enhances the ability of μ-opioid receptors (μ-ORs) to inhibit the release of GABA in the PAG, which is mediated via an enhanced coupling of μ-ORs to adenylyl-cyclase and protein kinase A (PKA) signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic opioid treatment causes an increase in the efficacy of μ-receptors on inhibitory nerve terminals in the PAG, and this may contribute to some of the behavioral signs of withdrawal.
the opioid receptor in the PAG becomes more effective in producing presynaptic inhibition after chronic opioid treatment.
chronic opioid exposure induces a long-term adaptation in GABAergic synaptic neurotransmission in PAG.
